_comment: Cross-source pairs for the conflict matrix (Milestone 5D-2).
WHAT IS REAL AND WHAT IS CONSTRUCTED — stated per entry in `origin` below,
because the difference matters. `measured` entries are values read from the
live Intellicar dashboard and the loaded telemetry database on 2026-08-03.
`constructed` entries are built to reach states this deployment's data
CANNOT produce, and each says which real value it is derived from.
WHY ANY ENTRY NEEDS CONSTRUCTING. The telemetry sample ends 2026-06-17 and
the portal is live now, so every real pair is about seven weeks apart. At
that separation the plausible-change bound is enormous and every difference
is explained by age — which is the CORRECT verdict, and which means the
`unexplained` path is unreachable from real data. It is the path that
matters most in production, so it is exercised here instead. Milestone 5C
recorded the same kind of admission about degradation trends: the data
cannot support them, and that is reported rather than worked around.
The `unknownAge` entry is not hypothetical. Last Talk Time renders as a raw
epoch before the page formats it, so a live reading with no measurement
time was observed on 200 of 320 rows in one pass. It is the reason
AgeExplanation has three states rather than two.

agreeingSpeed.note: The one genuine cross-source pair in this deployment. Live speed 0 km/h against the newest recorded GPS speed 0.23 km/h, 47.1 days apart. Difference 0.23 < threshold 2, so the two AGREE and no conflict is reported.

explainedPosition.note: The same real pair, on position. Live (25.433566, 82.108989) against the newest recorded fix (25.433644, 82.108320). 67.7 m apart — above the 50 m threshold, so a conflict IS detected — but 1131 hours at 120 km/h could account for roughly 135,000 km, so it is explained by age and the value is not disputed.

unexplainedPosition.note: Two REAL positions of this vehicle — the live one, and a real GPS fix from its own series — placed ONE MINUTE apart. They are 2401.4 m apart (verified independently), while one minute at 120 km/h accounts for at most 2000 m: the vehicle would have had to average 144 km/h. Note how narrow the margin is, and that it had to be engineered: at a five-minute gap the same 2401 m is comfortably explained, which is why this entry uses one.

unexplainedSpeed.note: Two real speeds from this vehicle's own GPS series (27.20 and 0.03 km/h) placed one second apart. 27.17 km/h of change in one second exceeds what 3600 km/h per hour allows, so the difference is larger than the elapsed time explains.

unknownAge.note: The unexplainedSpeed pair with the live measurement time removed, which is what a row whose Last Talk Time had not yet been formatted actually produces. The difference still exceeds the threshold, so a conflict is reported — but plausibility cannot be assessed, so it is `unknown` and is NOT escalated to disputed.

withinScatter.note: Two consecutive real fixes taken while the vehicle was effectively stationary, 5.14 m apart (verified independently). Stationary scatter across the whole series peaks at 11.26 m, and the 50 m threshold was calibrated to sit above that — so a parked vehicle does not report a conflict with itself.
